atomicity.reason: One obligation: set the isolation fault when isolation resistance divided by pack voltage is below 500 ohm/V; the closing sentence only explains why a ratio is used.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: 'isolation resistance', 'pack voltage' and the ISO reference are ordinary HV-safety vocabulary and the ratio rationale is stated.

feasibility.reason: A ratio of a measured insulation resistance to a measured pack voltage is routine (insulation measurement circuit plus the pack-voltage channel) and the requirement conflicts with nothing else stated.

parent_fit.reason: Matches US_ISOLATION_MONITORING: the pack raises an isolation fault whenever the barrier is below the minimum for its voltage; the requirement turns that into a per-volt ratio and states the figure.

unambiguity.reason: The 500 ohm/V figure is explicit, but it is justified as 'the minimum ISO 6469-1 requires of a DC high-voltage system', which does not obviously match the figure: UN R100 (checked via a secondary source) sets 100 ohm/V for galvanically separate DC buses and 500 ohm/V for AC or combined buses, and I recall ISO 6469-3 aligning with that. I could not verify ISO 6469-1 itself, so which value the citation implies is uncertain.
unambiguity.suggestion: Check the clause and value against the standard, cite the exact part, clause and bus class (DC versus AC or combined), and keep the number and the citation consistent.

verifiability.reason: Inputs, formula, unit, threshold and strict comparison are explicit (R_iso / V_pack < 500 ohm/V), so a bench or HIL test can drive resistance and voltage pairs either side of the line and observe the fault.

summary: Crisp, parent-aligned ratio rule that is testable as written; the cited 'ISO 6469-1 DC minimum of 500 ohm/V' needs checking against the standard.
